prompt: A trip is $300$ miles long. Your average speed in miles per hour is $s(t) = \frac{300}{t}$, where $t$ is the number of hours the trip takes. If the trip takes $5$ hours, what is your average speed?
hint: The rule turns trip time into average speed. Which number should replace $t$ for this trip?

hints.text: The rule turns trip time into average speed. Which number should replace $t$ for this trip?
Put $5$ hours in place of $t$ to get $\frac{300}{5}$, then carry out the division $300 \div 5$.
Since $300 \div 5 = 60$, the average speed is $60$ miles per hour.

explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time, which is exactly what the rule $s(t) = \frac{300}{t}$ says.
The trip takes $5$ hours, so substitute to get $s(5) = \frac{300}{5}$.
Dividing gives $300 \div 5 = 60$, so the average speed is $60$ miles per hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Split the trip into hours
steps: Five equal hours must share the 300 miles.
Each hour carries the same chunk of road.
$300$ miles $\div$ 5 chunks $= 60$ miles in each hour.
